To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mice genetically lacking GPR88 show impairments in working memory, cognitive inflexibility and altered reward evaluation.
mice genetically deficient for the orphan receptor GPR88 show impairments in working memory and cognitive flexibility, and that they are hyperactive and show altered reward processing.

1) GPR88 KO mice have impaired performance in a touchscreen based radial 8-arm maze N-back task, consistent with a role of striatal GPR8 receptors in working memory; 2) GPR88 is also required for cognitive flexibility as evidenced by impaired reversal learning performance in the touchscreen task; 3) GPR88 receptors are also involved in reward processing as evidenced by enhanced motivation and risk taking in the touchscreen based Iowa gambling task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of schizophrenia, a severe psychiatric disorder.
understanding how the striatum, a key structure in reward processing, is influenced by genetic variation.
understanding the role of the striatal GPR receptor, GPR88, in the control of behaviour and cognition in mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GPR88 receptors are important in a range of cognitive processes, including working memory, reward processing, cognitive flexibility and motivational processes.

the GPR88 receptor plays an important role in a number of cortico striatal loops, and that this is likely to be mediated through its actions in the striatum, where GPR88 receptors are most highly expressed.

genetic deletion of Gpr88 leads to a complex behavioural phenotype that is consistent with a key role for striatal GPR8 receptors in the modulation of activity in a range or cortico striatal circuits, including those involved in working memory, cognitive inflexibility, reward processing and motor function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GPR88 receptors are important for the function of multiple cortico striato thalamic circuits, including those involved in cognition, motivation and reward evaluation.

the striatal receptor GPR88 plays an important role in the function of multiple cortico striato thalamic circuits, including those involved in cognitive function, reward processing and motor function.
the absence of GPR88 leads to a cognitive and reward processing phenotype in mice, which may be of relevance to human psychiatric disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Gpr88 KO animals have altered performance across a range of tasks that interrogate cognitive function and reward processing.
GPR88 is involved in cognitive flexibility, working memory and motivation, and that it may be an interesting target to study in psychiatric conditions such as schizophrenia.
GPR88 is a novel regulator of multiple aspects of cognition and reward processing.
